title: I made a trailer for my dwarf fighting game
author: BeautifulPut4684
selftext:
I went down a fantasy rabbit hole and started building a fantasy dwarf fighting game. I built it using GPT 5.6 Sol and Fable 5.

All sprites and assets where generated with Gemini and the music and SFXs where from Envato. 

Voices where made with Elevenlabs.

The original characters looked completely different. I ended up redesigning them after I found these Viking dwarf puppets on Amazon and got the idea to make a trailer for the game.

**I'm not entirely sure if the multiplayer works, but I guess I'm about to find out.**

Try out the game :) [https://bash.tv/richard/dwarf-bash?\_\_preview=1](https://bash.tv/richard/dwarf-bash?__preview=1)

replies.author: Atmic
replies.body:
Forget the concept of "quick game development done with AI", and embrace the concept of "quality game development aided by AI".

Really think about the gameplay loops and features. The art direction and assets. The story, if it's important. What makes the game unique and fun.

...and devote as much time as needed to get each to top-tier level. 

AI can assist with every step of the progress, but break it all down to the minutiae and build it back up. 

Then polish, polish, polish. 

If it takes a month, a year, it doesn't matter until it's where it needs to be. 

Just think: if AI could get you this far in one day, imagine what *doing it right* might look like.
